Joshua.author: Joshua, by Jewish tradition; the book says that "Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God" (Joshua 24:26). Notes about things that remain "unto this day" show that some parts were added later.
Joshua.audience: Israel after Moses, entering and settling Canaan.
Joshua.purpose: To recount Israel's entrance into the promised land, the distribution of territory, and the call to covenant faithfulness.
Joshua.theme: God is faithful to his promises, and his people are called to courageous, exclusive covenant loyalty.
Joshua.summary: Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan, through major campaigns, into tribal allotments, and finally calls the nation to choose faithful service to the LORD.

movements.title: Crossing the Jordan and Jericho
movements.description: Israel enters Canaan and captures Jericho after crossing the Jordan.

movements.title: Conquest Campaigns
movements.description: Israel experiences both failure at Ai and later victories as major opposition is subdued.

movements.title: Land Allotment and Covenant Renewal
movements.description: The land is apportioned among tribes, and Joshua renews the covenant at Shechem.

keyFigures.name: Joshua
keyFigures.description: Moses' successor, who leads Israel across the Jordan, through the conquest, and in covenant renewal at Shechem.

keyFigures.name: Rahab
keyFigures.description: A Canaanite woman of Jericho who hides the Israelite spies and is spared with her family.

keyFigures.name: Achan
keyFigures.description: Takes devoted plunder from Jericho, causing Israel's defeat at Ai.

keyFigures.name: Caleb
keyFigures.description: One of the faithful spies, who at eighty-five claims Hebron as his inheritance.

keyFigures.name: The Gibeonites
keyFigures.description: A Canaanite people who deceive Israel into making a peace treaty.

keyFigures.name: Adonizedek
keyFigures.description: King of Jerusalem who leads a coalition of kings against Gibeon and Israel.

keyFigures.name: Eleazar
keyFigures.description: The high priest who helps Joshua distribute the land among the tribes.

Judges.author: Samuel, according to Jewish tradition. The book does not name its writer, and its refrain "In those days there was no king in Israel" shows it was written after Israel had kings.
Judges.audience: Israel during the period between Joshua and the monarchy.
Judges.purpose: To explain Israel's recurring cycle of apostasy, oppression, crying out, and deliverance, while showing the need for faithful leadership.
Judges.theme: When God's people abandon covenant faithfulness, disorder deepens; God repeatedly shows mercy through deliverers.
Judges.summary: Judges tells a downward spiral: Israel turns from God, suffers oppression, cries out, and is rescued by judges. The book becomes increasingly dark and ends with social and moral chaos.

movements.title: Early Cycles of the Judges
movements.description: Figures such as Othniel, Ehud, and Deborah deliver Israel from oppressors.

movements.title: Gideon and Jephthah
movements.description: Later judges show both God's deliverance and the growing flaws of Israel's leaders.

movements.title: Samson and National Disorder
movements.description: Samson's troubled judgeship is followed by stories of idolatry, violence, and civil war.

keyFigures.name: Othniel
keyFigures.description: Caleb's nephew and the first judge, who delivers Israel from a Mesopotamian king.

keyFigures.name: Ehud
keyFigures.description: A left-handed Benjaminite who assassinates Eglon, king of Moab.

keyFigures.name: Deborah
keyFigures.description: A prophetess and judge who summons Barak to lead Israel against the Canaanite army.

keyFigures.name: Barak
keyFigures.description: The military leader who defeats Sisera's forces alongside Deborah.

keyFigures.name: Jael
keyFigures.description: A Kenite woman who kills the fleeing commander Sisera.

keyFigures.name: Gideon
keyFigures.description: Called while hiding from the Midianites, he defeats them with only three hundred men.

keyFigures.name: Abimelech
keyFigures.description: Gideon's son, who seizes power by murdering his brothers and dies violently.

keyFigures.name: Jephthah
keyFigures.description: A rejected son who delivers Israel from the Ammonites but makes a tragic vow.

keyFigures.name: Samson
keyFigures.description: A Nazarite of great strength whose personal failings, including with Delilah, end in his capture and death among the Philistines.

Ruth.author: Anonymous; Jewish tradition has sometimes associated it with Samuel.
Ruth.audience: Israel, likely with special interest in David's ancestry and covenant faithfulness.
Ruth.purpose: To show God's providence, loyal love, and the inclusion of a Moabite woman in the family line that leads to David.
Ruth.theme: God works through ordinary faithfulness, kindness, and providence to bring redemption.
Ruth.summary: Ruth follows Naomi and her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth from grief and poverty to restoration. Ruth's loyalty leads to marriage with Boaz, and their family line becomes part of David's ancestry.

movements.title: Ruth Chooses Naomi and Israel's God
movements.description: After the deaths of their husbands, Ruth refuses to abandon Naomi and returns with her to Bethlehem.

movements.title: Ruth Meets Boaz
movements.description: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field and receives protection and kindness.

movements.title: Redemption and Family Restoration
movements.description: Boaz acts as kinsman-redeemer, marries Ruth, and their son Obed becomes grandfather of David.

keyFigures.name: Naomi
keyFigures.description: An Israelite widow who returns from Moab to Bethlehem in bitterness and is restored.

keyFigures.name: Ruth
keyFigures.description: Naomi's Moabite daughter-in-law, whose loyalty leads her to Bethlehem and into David's ancestry.

keyFigures.name: Boaz
keyFigures.description: A worthy relative of Naomi's family who acts as kinsman-redeemer and marries Ruth.

keyFigures.name: Elimelech
keyFigures.description: Naomi's husband, who moves the family to Moab during a famine and dies there.

keyFigures.name: Orpah
keyFigures.description: Naomi's other daughter-in-law, who returns to her own people in Moab.

keyFigures.name: Obed
keyFigures.description: The son of Ruth and Boaz; father of Jesse and grandfather of David.

1 Samuel.author: Anonymous; traditions connect material with Samuel, Nathan, and Gad, but the final form is later than Samuel's lifetime.
1 Samuel.audience: Israel during the transition from judges to monarchy.
1 Samuel.purpose: To recount the rise of the monarchy, the failure of Saul, and the emergence of David as God's chosen king.
1 Samuel.theme: God looks at the heart, resists proud leadership, and advances His purposes through faithful obedience.
1 Samuel.summary: 1 Samuel moves from Samuel's birth and prophetic ministry to Saul's rise and fall, then to David's anointing and long conflict with Saul.

movements.title: Samuel's Rise
movements.description: Samuel is born, called by God, and becomes a prophet and judge during a period of priestly corruption.

movements.title: Saul Becomes King and Fails
movements.description: Israel asks for a king; Saul is chosen but repeatedly disobeys God's commands.

movements.title: David's Rise
movements.description: David is anointed, defeats Goliath, and becomes Saul's rival while refusing to seize the throne by force.

keyFigures.name: Hannah
keyFigures.description: A barren woman who prays for a son, dedicates Samuel to the LORD, and sings a song of praise.

keyFigures.name: Eli
keyFigures.description: Priest at Shiloh, whose corrupt sons Hophni and Phinehas bring judgment on his household.

keyFigures.name: Samuel
keyFigures.description: Prophet, priest, and last judge of Israel, who anoints both Saul and David.

keyFigures.name: Saul
keyFigures.description: Israel's first king, who begins well but is rejected by God for disobedience.

keyFigures.name: Jonathan
keyFigures.description: Saul's son, a brave warrior and loyal friend to David.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.description: A shepherd anointed as future king, who defeats Goliath and flees from Saul's jealousy.

keyFigures.name: Goliath
keyFigures.description: The Philistine champion from Gath defeated by David.

keyFigures.name: Abigail
keyFigures.description: A wise woman who prevents David from taking revenge on her foolish husband Nabal, and later becomes David's wife.

2 Samuel.author: Anonymous; built from royal and prophetic traditions.
2 Samuel.audience: Israel under David's reign and later readers reflecting on the Davidic monarchy.
2 Samuel.purpose: To narrate David's reign, God's covenant promise to his house, and the serious consequences of David's sin.
2 Samuel.theme: God establishes David's dynasty, yet even the chosen king is accountable for sin and its consequences.
2 Samuel.summary: David becomes king over all Israel, captures Jerusalem, receives God's covenant promise, and experiences both great victories and deep family turmoil after his sin with Bathsheba.

movements.title: David Becomes King
movements.description: David is first king over Judah and then over all Israel; Jerusalem becomes his capital.

movements.title: The Davidic Covenant
movements.description: God promises David an enduring dynasty and future royal line.

movements.title: David's Sin and Family Crisis
movements.description: David's adultery and arranged killing are followed by conflict, rebellion, and grief within his household.

keyFigures.name: David
keyFigures.description: Becomes king over Judah and then all Israel, receives God's covenant promise, but sins grievously with Bathsheba.

keyFigures.name: Ish-bosheth
keyFigures.description: Saul's son, set up as a rival king over Israel before his assassination.

keyFigures.name: Joab
keyFigures.description: Commander of David's army, effective but often ruthless.

keyFigures.name: Mephibosheth
keyFigures.description: Jonathan's disabled son, to whom David shows covenant kindness.

keyFigures.name: Bathsheba
keyFigures.description: Wife of Uriah, taken by David; later mother of Solomon.

keyFigures.name: Uriah the Hittite
keyFigures.description: A loyal soldier whom David arranges to have killed in battle.

keyFigures.name: Nathan
keyFigures.description: The prophet who delivers the Davidic covenant and later confronts David's sin with a parable.

keyFigures.name: Absalom
keyFigures.description: David's son, who kills his brother Amnon and later leads a rebellion against his father.

1 Kings.author: Anonymous; often understood as part of a larger historical work compiled from earlier royal records and prophetic sources.
1 Kings.audience: Judah and Israel, especially readers reflecting on the monarchy and exile.
1 Kings.purpose: To explain the history of the united and divided kingdoms in light of covenant faithfulness and failure.
1 Kings.theme: The health of the kingdom is measured by loyalty to the LORD; idolatry and disobedience lead toward judgment.
1 Kings.summary: Solomon builds the temple but later compromises through idolatry. After his death the kingdom divides, and prophetic voices such as Elijah confront royal unfaithfulness.

movements.title: Solomon's Reign and Temple
movements.description: Solomon receives wisdom, builds the temple, and reaches great prosperity.

movements.title: Kingdom Divides
movements.description: Solomon's later idolatry is followed by the split between Israel in the north and Judah in the south.

movements.title: Elijah Confronts Ahab
movements.description: Elijah challenges Baal worship and the policies of Ahab and Jezebel.

keyFigures.name: Solomon
keyFigures.description: David's son and successor, renowned for wisdom, who builds the temple but later turns to idolatry.

keyFigures.name: Adonijah
keyFigures.description: David's son, who attempts to seize the throne before Solomon is crowned.

keyFigures.name: The Queen of Sheba
keyFigures.description: A foreign ruler who visits Solomon to test his wisdom and praises Israel's God.

keyFigures.name: Rehoboam
keyFigures.description: Solomon's son, whose harsh policy prompts the northern tribes to break away.

keyFigures.name: Jeroboam
keyFigures.description: First king of the northern kingdom, who sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

keyFigures.name: Ahab
keyFigures.description: King of Israel who promotes Baal worship and opposes Elijah.

keyFigures.name: Jezebel
keyFigures.description: Ahab's Phoenician wife, who persecutes the LORD's prophets and arranges Naboth's murder.

keyFigures.name: Elijah
keyFigures.description: The prophet who confronts Ahab, defeats the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, and hears God's quiet voice at Horeb.

2 Kings.author: Anonymous; likely compiled from royal, prophetic, and historical sources.
2 Kings.audience: Judah and Israel, especially communities seeking to understand why both kingdoms fell.
2 Kings.purpose: To trace the decline and exile of Israel and Judah as the result of persistent covenant rebellion, while preserving signs of God's prophetic faithfulness.
2 Kings.theme: Persistent idolatry and injustice bring covenant judgment, yet God's word continues to prove reliable.
2 Kings.summary: 2 Kings records prophetic ministries, royal reforms, repeated rebellion, the fall of Samaria, and finally the fall of Jerusalem and exile to Babylon.

movements.title: Elijah's Departure and Elisha's Ministry
movements.description: Elijah is taken up, and Elisha carries on a powerful prophetic ministry.

movements.title: Fall of the Northern Kingdom
movements.description: After generations of idolatry, Assyria captures Samaria and exiles Israel.

movements.title: Judah's Last Kings and Exile
movements.description: Despite reforms under Hezekiah and Josiah, Judah eventually falls to Babylon and Jerusalem is destroyed.

keyFigures.name: Elijah
keyFigures.description: Taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, passing his ministry to Elisha.

keyFigures.name: Elisha
keyFigures.description: Elijah's successor, whose ministry is marked by many miracles.

keyFigures.name: Naaman
keyFigures.description: An Aramean army commander healed of a skin disease after washing in the Jordan.

keyFigures.name: Jehu
keyFigures.description: Anointed king of Israel, who destroys Ahab's dynasty and Baal worship.

keyFigures.name: Hezekiah
keyFigures.description: A reforming king of Judah who trusts God when Assyria besieges Jerusalem.

keyFigures.name: Isaiah
keyFigures.description: The prophet who counsels Hezekiah during the Assyrian crisis and his illness.

keyFigures.name: Sennacherib
keyFigures.description: King of Assyria, whose army threatens Jerusalem but is struck down.

keyFigures.name: Manasseh
keyFigures.description: Hezekiah's son, whose long and idolatrous reign is blamed for Judah's coming judgment.

keyFigures.name: Josiah
keyFigures.description: A king who leads sweeping reforms after the Book of the Law is found in the temple.

keyFigures.name: Nebuchadnezzar
keyFigures.description: King of Babylon, who conquers Judah, destroys Jerusalem, and carries the people into exile.
